5. Existing JVM text/signal tests.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.1.5</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-render-html</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>Pathland Render HTML</name>
    <description>
        The Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer (dev.pathland.render.html): a
        thin JNA shim over libpathland_render_html (pathland_html_render /
        _render_fragment / _free). Stateless: each call renders
        a full snapshot frame to HTML in one pass. The server-side/remote-projection
        target, usable from Spring Boot, Quarkus, or any Java server. The single
        renderer is the Rust crate reused by every language.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>net.java.dev.jna</groupId>
            <artifactId>jna</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals><goal>test-compile</goal></goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <!-- Point the test JVM at the Rust renderer cdylib; absent the
                         dylib, the shim tests are skipped via an assumption. -->
                    <argLine>-Djava.library.path=${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug</argLine>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

            <!-- Embed the Rust renderer dylib in the jar so it travels with the
                 artifact (JNA extracts it at runtime — no java.library.path needed).
                 Copies the host-platform build into META-INF/native/. Fails loudly
                 when the dylib is missing (the CI rust job builds it; locally run
                 cargo build first). -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-antrun-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>embed-native-renderer</id>
                        <phase>process-resources</phase>
                        <configuration>
                            <target>
                                <!-- Determine the platform library extension. -->
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".dylib">
                                    <os family="mac" />
                                </condition>
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".dll">
                                    <os family="windows" />
                                </condition>
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".so">
                                    <os family="unix" />
                                </condition>
                                <property name="pathland.native.ext" value="" />

                                <!-- Release builds stage one lib per platform under
                                     target/native/<os>-<arch>/ (the CI matrix) and
                                     this copies each into META-INF/native/<os>-<arch>/.
                                     A local build has no staging dir and instead
                                     embeds the host Rust debug build in the flat
                                     META-INF/native/ layout. -->
                                <property name="pathland.native.staging" value="${project.basedir}/target/native" />
                                <available file="${pathland.native.staging}" type="dir" property="pathland.native.staged" />
                                <property name="pathland.native.host" value="${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html${pathland.native.ext}" />
                                <available file="${pathland.native.host}" property="pathland.native.host.present" />

                                <fail message="No Rust renderer library to embed: neither per-platform libs at ${pathland.native.staging}/<os>-<arch>/ (release) nor the host build at ${pathland.native.host} (local). Build it first: cargo build -p pathland-render-html (in lib/rust).">
                                    <condition>
                                        <and>
                                            <not><isset property="pathland.native.staged" /></not>
                                            <not><isset property="pathland.native.host.present" /></not>
                                        </and>
                                    </condition>
                                </fail>

                                <mkdir dir="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native" />
                                <!-- Release: copy each staged platform dir verbatim. -->
                                <copy todir="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native">
                                    <fileset dir="${pathland.native.staging}" includes="*/*" erroronmissingdir="false" />
                                </copy>
                                <!-- Local dev: embed the host lib in the flat layout. -->
                                <copy file="${pathland.native.host}"
                                      tofile="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native/libpathland_render_html${pathland.native.ext}"
                                      failonerror="false" />
                            </target>
                        </configuration>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>run</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

# pathland-view-core (JVM engine + DSL) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 5, 2026

The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the
Pathland protocol, written entirely in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared
authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter,
signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform state, JNA ring
interop, and the `dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers.
Server and renderer modules depend on this one module; Java hosts consume the
Kotlin-authored views through JVM interop.

## Implemented

- **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
  `Commands`, `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`, `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`,
  `TokenPath`.
- **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/
  `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
  caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
  `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState`
  during a component render.
- **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped
  `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates
  bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and
  annotation processor are removed.
- **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
  `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
- **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
  `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
  `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` and the navigation helpers live in the Kotlin DSL.
- **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
  `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
- **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
  `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
  Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding

25:         writeHeader(out, GUEST_TO_HOST, sequence, frame.opcodes.size)
26:         for (op in frame.opcodes) {
27:             writeBytes(out, op.toBytes())

34:     /** Decode a self-contained frame batch into opcodes + string section. */
35:     @JvmStatic
36:     fun decodeFrame(bytes: ByteArray): ProtocolFrame {
37:         val parsed = parse(bytes)
38:         return ProtocolFrame(parsed.opcodes, parsed.strings)
39:     }

41:     /** The per-stream message sequence encoded in a batch header (offset 8). */
42:     @JvmStatic
43:     fun sequence(bytes: ByteArray): Int {
44:         if (bytes.size < HEADER) throw IllegalArgumentException("batch truncated")
45:         return readIntLE(bytes, 8)
46:     }

48:     /** Encode a `META::RESYNC` request batch (host → guest). */

52:     /** Encode a `META::PONG` reply batch (host → guest). */
53:     @JvmStatic
54:     fun encodePong(): ByteArray = singleMeta(Commands.Meta.PONG)

56:     /** Encode a `META::PING` heartbeat probe batch (guest → host). */

62:         writeIntLE(out, 0)
63:         return out.toByteArray()

66:     private fun singleMeta(command: Int): ByteArray {
67:         val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
68:         writeHeader(out, HOST_TO_GUEST, 0, 1)

70:         writeIntLE(out, 0)

74:     /** Encode a `META::ENVIRONMENT` field batch (viewport + route). */
75:     @JvmStatic
76:     fun encodeEnvironment(env: EnvironmentData): ByteArray {
77:         val route = env.route.toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
78:         val ops = ArrayList<Opcode>(3)
79:         if (env.viewportWidth > 0) {

90:         writeHeader(out, HOST_TO_GUEST, 0, ops.size)
91:         for (op in ops) {

106:     @JvmStatic

111:     @JvmStatic

119:         var route: String? = null
120:         var width = -1f
121:         var height = -1f
122:         for (op in parsed.opcodes) {
123:             if (op.category != Categories.META || op.command != Commands.Meta.ENVIRONMENT) continue
124:             when (op.a and 0xFFFF) {
125:                 Commands.Environment.VIEWPORT_WIDTH -> width = Float.fromBits(op.b)
126:                 Commands.Environment.VIEWPORT_HEIGHT -> height = Float.fromBits(op.b)

128:             }

133:     /** Encode host → guest events as a batch. */
134:     @JvmStatic
135:     fun encodeEvents(events: List<Event>): ByteArray {
136:         val opcodes = ArrayList<Opcode>(events.size)
137:         val strings = ByteArrayOutputStream()
138:         for (event in events) {
139:             when {
140:                 event.isTextChanged -> {
141:                     val offset = strings.size()
142:                     val utf8 = event.text.orEmpty().toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
143:                     writeIntLE(strings, utf8.size)
144:                     strings.writeBytes(utf8)
145:                     opcodes.add(Opcode(
146:                         Categories.EVENT, Commands.Event.TEXT_CHANGED, 0, event.target, offset, 0))
147:                 }
148:                 event.isNavigate -> {
149:                     if (event.isNavigateBack) {
150:                         opcodes.add(Opcode(Categories.EVENT, Commands.Event.NAVIGATE, 0, 0, 0, 0))
151:                     } else {
152:                         val offset = strings.size()
153:                         val utf8 = event.url().orEmpty().toByteArray(StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
154:                         writeIntLE(strings, utf8.size)
155:                         strings.writeBytes(utf8)
156:                         opcodes.add(Opcode(
157:                             Categories.EVENT, Commands.Event.NAVIGATE, Commands.Flags.NAVIGATE_URL, 0, offset, 0))
158:                     }
159:                 }
160:                 event.isValueChanged -> opcodes.add(Opcode(
161:                     Categories.EVENT, Commands.Event.VALUE_CHANGED, 0,
162:                     event.target, event.value.toRawBits(), 0))
163:                 event.isKeyDown || event.isKeyUp -> opcodes.add(Opcode(
164:                     Categories.EVENT, event.command, event.flags, event.target, event.b, event.c))
165:                 event.isDateChanged -> opcodes.add(Opcode(
166:                     Categories.EVENT, Commands.Event.DATE_CHANGED, 0, event.target, event.b, event.c))
167:                 event.isFocusChanged || event.isEditingChanged || event.isSubmit -> opcodes.add(Opcode(
168:                     Categories.EVENT, event.command, 0, event.target, event.b, 0))
169:                 event.isMediaTimeUpdated || event.isMediaVolumeChanged ||
170:                     event.isMediaDurationChanged || event.isFitChanged -> opcodes.add(Opcode(
171:                     Categories.EVENT, event.command, 0, event.target, event.value.toRawBits(), 0))
172:                 event.isMediaPlayStateChanged || event.isMediaEnded -> opcodes.add(Opcode(
173:                     Categories.EVENT, event.command, 0, event.target, event.b, 0))
174:                 else -> opcodes.add(Opcode(
175:                     Categories.EVENT, event.command, event.flags, event.target,
176:                     event.x.toRawBits(), event.y.toRawBits()))
177:             }
178:         }
179:         val out = ByteArrayOutputStream()
180:         writeHeader(out, HOST_TO_GUEST, 0, opcodes.size)
181:         for (op in opcodes) {
182:             writeBytes(out, op.toBytes())
183:         }
184:         writeIntLE(out, strings.size())
185:         writeBytes(out, strings.toByteArray())
186:         return out.toByteArray()
187:     }
188: 
189:     /** Decode a host → guest event batch into typed events. */
190:     @JvmStatic
191:     fun decodeEvents(bytes: ByteArray): List<Event> {
192:         val parsed = parse(bytes)
193:         val events = ArrayList<Event>()
194:         for (op in parsed.opcodes) {
195:             if (op.category != Categories.EVENT) continue
196:             when (op.command) {
197:                 Commands.Event.TEXT_CHANGED -> events.add(Event.textChanged(op.a, parsed.stringAt(op.b)))
198:                 Commands.Event.NAVIGATE -> events.add(
199:                     if ((op.flags and Commands.Flags.NAVIGATE_URL) != 0) {
200:                         Event.navigate(parsed.stringAt(op.b))
201:                     } else {
202:                         Event.navigateBack()
203:                     })
204:                 Commands.Event.VALUE_CHANGED -> events.add(Event.valueChanged(op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b)))
205:                 Commands.Event.KEY_DOWN -> events.add(Event.keyDown(op.a, op.b, op.c, op.flags))
206:                 Commands.Event.KEY_UP -> events.add(Event.keyUp(op.a, op.b, op.c))
207:                 Commands.Event.DATE_CHANGED -> events.add(Event.dateChanged(op.a, op.b, op.c))
208:                 Commands.Event.FOCUS_CHANGED -> events.add(Event.focusChanged(op.a, op.b != 0))
209:                 Commands.Event.EDITING_CHANGED -> events.add(Event.editingChanged(op.a, op.b != 0))
210:                 Commands.Event.SUBMIT -> events.add(Event.submit(op.a))
211:                 Commands.Event.SCROLL -> events.add(Event.scroll(
212:                     op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b), Float.fromBits(op.c)))
213:                 Commands.Event.WHEEL -> events.add(Event.wheel(
214:                     op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b), Float.fromBits(op.c)))
215:                 Commands.Event.MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED -> events.add(
216:                     Event.mediaPlayStateChanged(op.a, op.b != 0))
217:                 Commands.Event.MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED -> events.add(
218:                     Event.mediaTimeUpdated(op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b)))
219:                 Commands.Event.MEDIA_ENDED -> events.add(Event.mediaEnded(op.a))
220:                 Commands.Event.MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED -> events.add(
221:                     Event.mediaVolumeChanged(op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b)))
222:                 Commands.Event.MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED -> events.add(
223:                     Event.mediaDurationChanged(op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b)))
224:                 Commands.Event.FIT_CHANGED -> events.add(
225:                     Event.fitChanged(op.a, Float.fromBits(op.b)))
226:                 Commands.Event.POINTER_DOWN, Commands.Event.POINTER_MOVE, Commands.Event.POINTER_UP ->
227:                     events.add(Event(op.command, op.a, op.flags, Float.fromBits(op.b),
228:                         Float.fromBits(op.c), 0f, null, 0, 0))
229:             }
230:         }
231:         return events
232:     }
233: 
234:     private class Parsed(val opcodes: List<Opcode>, val strings: ByteArray) {
235:         fun stringAt(offset: Int): String {
236:             val len = (strings[offset].toInt() and 0xFF) or
237:                 ((strings[offset + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
238:                 ((strings[offset + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
239:                 ((strings[offset + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
240:             return String(strings, offset + 4, len, StandardCharsets.UTF_8)
241:         }
242:     }
243: 
244:     private fun parse(bytes: ByteArray): Parsed {
245:         if (bytes.size < HEADER) throw IllegalArgumentException("batch truncated")
246:         val magic = readIntLE(bytes, 0)
247:         if (magic != MAGIC) {
248:             throw IllegalArgumentException("bad batch magic 0x${Integer.toHexString(magic)}")
249:         }
250:         val version = (bytes[4].toInt() and 0xFF) or ((bytes[5].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8)
251:         if (version != VERSION) {
252:             throw IllegalArgumentException("unsupported batch version $version")
253:         }
254:         val opcodeCount = readIntLE(bytes, 12)
255:         val opcodesEnd = HEADER + opcodeCount * Opcode.SIZE
256:         if (opcodesEnd + 4 > bytes.size) {
257:             throw IllegalArgumentException("batch truncated (opcodes)")
258:         }
259:         val opcodes = ArrayList<Opcode>(opcodeCount)
260:         for (i in 0 until opcodeCount) {
261:             val slot = ByteArray(Opcode.SIZE)
262:             System.arraycopy(bytes, HEADER + i * Opcode.SIZE, slot, 0, Opcode.SIZE)
263:             opcodes.add(Opcode.fromBytes(slot))
264:         }
265:         val stringsLen = readIntLE(bytes, opcodesEnd)
266:         val stringsStart = opcodesEnd + 4
267:         if (stringsStart + stringsLen > bytes.size) {
268:             throw IllegalArgumentException("batch truncated (strings)")
269:         }
270:         val strings = ByteArray(stringsLen)
271:         System.arraycopy(bytes, stringsStart, strings, 0, stringsLen)
272:         return Parsed(opcodes, strings)
273:     }
274: 
275:     private fun writeHeader(out: ByteArrayOutputStream, flags: Int, sequence: Int, opcodeCount: Int) {
276:         writeIntLE(out, MAGIC)
277:         writeShortLE(out, VERSION)
278:         writeShortLE(out, flags)
279:         writeIntLE(out, sequence)
280:         writeIntLE(out, opcodeCount)
281:     }
282: 
283:     private fun writeIntLE(out: ByteArrayOutputStream, value: Int) {
284:         out.write(value and 0xFF)
285:         out.write((value ushr 8) and 0xFF)
286:         out.write((value ushr 16) and 0xFF)
287:         out.write((value ushr 24) and 0xFF)
288:     }
289: 
290:     private fun writeShortLE(out: ByteArrayOutputStream, value: Int) {
291:         out.write(value and 0xFF)
292:         out.write((value ushr 8) and 0xFF)
293:     }
294: 
295:     private fun writeBytes(out: ByteArrayOutputStream, bytes: ByteArray) {
296:         out.writeBytes(bytes)
297:     }
298: 
299:     private fun readIntLE(bytes: ByteArray, offset: Int): Int =
300:         (bytes[offset].toInt() and 0xFF) or
301:             ((bytes[offset + 1].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 8) or
302:             ((bytes[offset + 2].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 16) or
303:             ((bytes[offset + 3].toInt() and 0xFF) shl 24)
304: }

package dev.pathland.view.core.protocol

/** Value types for `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY` (mirrors `pathland_core::value_type`). */
object ValueTypes {
    const val U8 = 0x01
    const val U32 = 0x02
    const val I32 = 0x03
    const val F32 = 0x04
    const val STRING = 0x05
    const val ENUM = 0x06
    const val COLOR = 0x07
    const val DESIGN_TOKEN = 0x08
    const val LIST = 0x09

    /** The protocol value type for a property id (mirrors `value_type_for`). */
    @JvmStatic
    fun forProperty(prop: Int): Int = when (prop) {
        Properties.COLOR, Properties.BACKGROUND_COLOR, Properties.BORDER_COLOR,

        Properties.TINT -> COLOR
        Properties.EVENT_LISTENERS, Properties.BORDER_EDGES -> U32

        Properties.FIXED_SIZE_HORIZONTAL, Properties.FIXED_SIZE_VERTICAL,
        Properties.MEDIA_MUTED, Properties.MEDIA_LOOP -> U8
        Properties.LABEL, Properties.PROMPT, Properties.FONT_FAMILY, Properties.IMAGE_SOURCE,
        Properties.MEDIA_SOURCE, Properties.ROUTE,
        Properties.ICON_NAME, Properties.GRID_TRACKS -> STRING
        Properties.LINE_LIMIT, Properties.SELECTION, Properties.ACTION_ID, Properties.BINDING_ID,
        Properties.NAV_DEPTH, Properties.PLAYBACK_STATE,
        Properties.MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID -> U32
        Properties.FIT_QUERY -> LIST

}

1: # pathland-render-html (Java) — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** October 28, 2026
4: 
5: The **Java binding to the Rust HTML renderer** (`dev.pathland.render.html`) — a
6: thin **JNA shim** over `libpathland_render_html`. There is a **single renderer**
7: (the Rust crate), reused by every language; the former hand-written retained
8: Java renderer is removed. Protocol contract: `spec/`.
9: 
10: ## Implemented
11: 
12: - **Stateless JNA shim**: `HtmlRenderer.instance()` links the Rust cdylib;
13:   `render(frame, root)` / `renderFragment(frame, root)` /
14:   `renderFullSnapshot(frame, root)` render a self-contained snapshot frame to
15:   HTML in one pass (no retained tree, no `applyFrame`); `pathland_html_free`
16:   releases native strings. Lazy-loaded; skipped (test assumption) when the dylib
17:   is absent from `java.library.path`.
18: - **Debug comments**: `renderDebug(frame, root)` / `renderFragmentDebug(...)`
19:   bind the Rust `pathland_html_render_debug` exports — each rendered node is
20:   prefixed with an HTML comment naming its component type and the modifiers
21:   applied (opt-in; the plain `render` output is unchanged).
22: - **Full Rust renderer surface** (canonical): all spec components render inline
23:   (structural + decorative CSS in a single `style` attribute), ARIA/event
24:   attributes, `IS_SECURE` → password, `TOGGLE_STYLE` variants,
25:   `DATE_PICKER_MODE`, and literal colors inline. The default `render(...)`
26:   injects the renderer's built-in `<style>` block (preflight reset + design
27:   tokens + `.pathland-*` component defaults) into every document — no
28:   `/tailwind.css`. `renderLinked(frame, root, cssBase)` /
29:   `renderLinkedDebug(...)` instead emit a content-hashed
30:   `<link rel="stylesheet" href="{cssBase}/{baseCssName()}">`; token overrides
31:   and fit-band rules stay inline. `baseCss()` / `baseCssName()` bind the Rust
32:   `pathland_html_base_css[_name]` exports so the Spring/Quarkus starters serve
33:   the renderer-owned bytes immutable. A missing linked export degrades to the
34:   inline document.
35: - **Icon glyphs from the shared renderer**: `iconSvg(String name)` binds the
36:   Rust `pathland_html_icon_svg` export over the C ABI — the full inline `<svg>`
37:   for a canonical `ICON_NAME` (unknown/extension names → the renderer's
38:   fallback glyph, never null). Hosts serve `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` from
39:   it (Spring/Quarkus route a few lines in their starters), so the DOM client's
40:   lazy icon fetch gets the same glyph data SSR inlines from — one Rust source,
41:   no per-platform static icon files. `HtmlRendererTest` covers it.
42: - **Demos use the shim**: `SessionApp` no longer calls `applyFrame`; SSR renders
43:   the mount frame through `HtmlRenderer.render(sink.frame(), rootId)`. The
44:   renderer is compiled once at startup.
45: - **Text fields share one component class**: `TEXT_FIELD` inputs and `TEXT_EDITOR`
46:   textareas render with `class="pathland-input"` (Tailwind-style inset-outline
47:   styling from the Rust renderer's CSS); the copied `@pathland/dom-renderer`
48:   bundle (content-hashed `dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` in both demos) mirrors the
49:   class so delta-created fields hydrate identically.
50: 
51: ## Removed (September 2026)
52: 
53: - `compileTailwind(overrideCss)` and the `pathland_tailwind_compile` binding are
54:   **deleted** — the renderer is inline-only now and needs no compiler. The demo
55:   `/tailwind.css` endpoints (`TailwindCssController` / `TailwindCssResource`)
56:   and the `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/tailwind.css">` in both `SessionApp`
57:   files are removed.
58: 
59: ## Not implemented / gaps
60: 
61: - **Typography uses the platform system font stack** (`system-ui,
62:   -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, …`) — the Rust renderer's document head
63:   makes no external/webfont requests, so the demo pages render without loading
64:   any font files and work offline. An app can still override `font.body.family`
65:   via a `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` to any font it hosts.
66: - The shim is unaffected by the Rust renderer's September 2026 shell alignment
67:   (SPACER/MENU/STEPPER/GAUGE/PICKER markup now matches the DOM client's runtime
68:   shells); the demos' SSR output reflects the Rust renderer as-is, pinned by the
69:   `pathland-html-golden` conformance harness. `HtmlRendererTest` covers the
70:   semantic-role → element mapping (`NAVIGATION`→`<nav>`, `HEADER`→`<h2>`,
71:   `TEXT_STYLE` headings) and the DSL's rejection of non-semantic role codes,
72:   plus media rendering (a `VIDEO` surface bound to its `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` —
73:   native `<video controls>` + `data-pathland-controller`, the non-visual hidden
74:   controller shell, image `alt` from the accessibility label,
75:   `ContentMode Fill`→`cover`).
76: 
77: ## Verified by
78: 
79: `mvn test -pl pathland-render-html` — JNA shim tests (skip when the Rust dylib
80: is absent), including the linked stylesheet link + `baseCss`/`baseCssName`
81: exposure; part of the non-demo reactor run on JDK 17.

1: //! Shared engine trace fixtures.
2: //!
3: //! Defines a small set of engine scenarios, runs the canonical Rust engine, and
4: //! writes each emitted frame as a self-contained PLPL batch in hex under
5: //! `spec/engine-traces/`. The Java engine test builds the same scenarios through
6: //! its DSL and compares its encoded frames byte-for-byte.
7: //!
8: //! This emits neutral wire data only (opcodes + strings in the existing batch
9: //! format). It does not contain Java source, packages, or formatting.
10: 
11: use pathland_core::{
12:     category, init_memory, parameter, value_type, Guest, Host, MemoryLayout, Opcode,
13: };
14: use pathland_core_transport::encode_frame;
15: use pathland_engine::{assign_ids, Component, Engine, Node, SignalId, SignalValue};
16: use std::fmt::Write as _;
17: use std::fs;
18: use std::io;
19: use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
20: 
21: fn trace_root() -> PathBuf {
22:     Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../../../spec/engine-traces")
23: }
24: 
25: fn text_node(text: &str) -> Node {
26:     Node::from_component(&Component::Text { text: text.into() })
27: }
28: 
29: fn vstack(children: Vec<Node>) -> Node {
30:     let mut node = Node::from_component(&Component::VStack);
31:     node.children = children;
32:     node
33: }
34: 
35: fn with_memory() -> (Vec<u8>, MemoryLayout) {
36:     let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
37:     let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
38:     init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
39:     (mem, layout)
40: }
41: 
42: fn note_arena_ref(frame: &pathland_core::Frame<'_>, offset: u32, max: &mut usize) {
43:     if let Ok(bytes) = frame.arena_get(offset) {
44:         *max = (*max).max(offset as usize + 4 + bytes.len());
45:     }
46: }
47: 
48: /// Trim the full arena region to the entries this frame references, matching the
49: /// compact string section a self-contained network batch carries.
50: fn used_arena(frame: &pathland_core::Frame<'_>) -> Vec<u8> {
51:     let mut max = 0usize;
52:     for op in frame.opcodes() {
53:         match (op.category(), op.command()) {
54:             (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_TEXT) => {
55:                 note_arena_ref(frame, op.b(), &mut max);
56:             }
57:             (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_PROPERTY) => {
58:                 let vt = (op.b() >> 16) as u8;
59:                 if vt == value_type::STRING
60:                     || vt == value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN
61:                     || vt == value_type::LIST
62:                 {
63:                     note_arena_ref(frame, op.c(), &mut max);
64:                 }
65:             }
66:             (category::PARAMETER, parameter::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) => {
67:                 note_arena_ref(frame, op.a(), &mut max);
68:                 if op.b() as u8 == value_type::STRING {
69:                     note_arena_ref(frame, op.c(), &mut max);
70:                 }
71:             }
72:             _ => {}
73:         }
74:     }
75:     frame.arena()[..max].to_vec()
76: }
77: 
78: fn read_frame(mem: &mut [u8], layout: &MemoryLayout) -> Vec<u8> {
79:     let mut host = Host::new(mem, layout);
80:     let frames = host.frames();
81:     let frame = frames.first().expect("expected one emitted frame");
82:     let opcodes: Vec<Opcode> = frame.opcodes().collect();
83:     let strings = used_arena(frame);
84:     encode_frame(&opcodes, &strings)
85: }
86: 
87: fn emit_frame(engine: &mut Engine, root: &Node) -> Vec<u8> {
88:     let (mut mem, layout) = with_memory();
89:     {
90:         let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
91:         guest.begin_frame();
92:         engine.emit(root, &mut guest).expect("emit");
93:         guest.end_frame();
94:     }
95:     read_frame(&mut mem, &layout)
96: }
97: 
98: fn signal_frame(engine: &mut Engine, signal: SignalId, value: SignalValue) -> Vec<u8> {
99:     let (mut mem, layout) = with_memory();
100:     {
101:         let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut mem, &layout);
102:         guest.begin_frame();
103:         engine
104:             .set_signal(signal, value, &mut guest)
105:             .expect("set signal");
106:         guest.end_frame();
107:     }
108:     read_frame(&mut mem, &layout)
109: }
110: 
111: struct Scenario {
112:     name: &'static str,
113:     steps: Vec<(&'static str, Vec<u8>)>,
114: }
115: 
116: fn mount_text_stack() -> Scenario {
117:     let mut engine = Engine::new();
118:     let mut root = vstack(vec![text_node("Hello")]);
119:     root.properties
120:         .insert(pathland_core::property_id::SPACING, 8.0f32.to_bits());
121:     assign_ids(&mut root, &mut 1);
122:     Scenario {
123:         name: "mount_text_stack",
124:         steps: vec![("000-mount", emit_frame(&mut engine, &root))],
125:     }
126: }
127: 
128: fn signal_text_delta() -> Scenario {
129:     let mut engine = Engine::new();
130:     let signal = engine.create_signal(SignalValue::Str("Hello".into()));
131:     let mut root = vstack(vec![text_node("Hello")]);
132:     root.children[0].text_binding = Some(signal);
133:     assign_ids(&mut root, &mut 1);
134: 
135:     let mount = emit_frame(&mut engine, &root);
136:     let delta = signal_frame(&mut engine, signal, SignalValue::Str("World".into()));
137:     Scenario {
138:         name: "signal_text_delta",
139:         steps: vec![("000-mount", mount), ("001-set-text", delta)],
140:     }
141: }
142: 
143: fn property_signal_delta() -> Scenario {
144:     let mut engine = Engine::new();
145:     let signal = engine.create_signal(SignalValue::F32(8.0));
146:     let mut root = vstack(vec![text_node("Hello")]);
147:     root.properties
148:         .insert(pathland_core::property_id::SPACING, 8.0f32.to_bits());
149:     root.property_bindings
150:         .insert(pathland_core::property_id::SPACING, signal);
151:     assign_ids(&mut root, &mut 1);
152: 
153:     let mount = emit_frame(&mut engine, &root);
154:     let delta = signal_frame(&mut engine, signal, SignalValue::F32(12.0));
155:     Scenario {
156:         name: "property_signal_delta",
157:         steps: vec![("000-mount", mount), ("001-set-spacing", delta)],
158:     }
159: }
160: 
161: fn styled_text_mount() -> Scenario {
162:     let mut engine = Engine::new();
163:     let mut root = text_node("Hello");
164:     root.properties
165:         .insert(pathland_core::property_id::FONT_SIZE, 17.0f32.to_bits());
166:     assign_ids(&mut root, &mut 1);
167:     Scenario {
168:         name: "styled_text_mount",
169:         steps: vec![("000-mount", emit_frame(&mut engine, &root))],
170:     }
171: }
172: 
173: fn structural_add_remove() -> Scenario {
174:     let mut engine = Engine::new();
175:     let mut root = vstack(vec![text_node("a")]);
176:     assign_ids(&mut root, &mut 1);
177:     let mount = emit_frame(&mut engine, &root);
178: 
179:     root.children.push(text_node("b"));
180:     assign_ids(&mut root, &mut 1);
181:     let added = emit_frame(&mut engine, &root);
182: 
183:     root.children.pop();
184:     let removed = emit_frame(&mut engine, &root);
185: 
186:     Scenario {
187:         name: "structural_add_remove",
188:         steps: vec![
189:             ("000-mount", mount),
190:             ("001-add-child", added),
191:             ("002-remove-child", removed),
192:         ],
193:     }
194: }
195: 
196: fn scenarios() -> Vec<Scenario> {
197:     vec![
198:         mount_text_stack(),
199:         signal_text_delta(),
200:         property_signal_delta(),
201:         styled_text_mount(),
202:         structural_add_remove(),
203:     ]
204: }
205: 
206: fn hex_file(scenario: &str, step: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
207:     let mut out = String::new();
208:     writeln!(
209:         out,
210:         "# Generated by `cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit` (lib/rust). Do not edit."
211:     )
212:     .unwrap();
213:     writeln!(out, "# scenario: {scenario}").unwrap();
214:     writeln!(out, "# step: {step}").unwrap();
215:     writeln!(
216:         out,
217:         "# format: self-contained PLPL batch bytes (lowercase hex)"
218:     )
219:     .unwrap();
220:     for chunk in bytes.chunks(32) {
221:         for byte in chunk {
222:             write!(out, "{byte:02x}").unwrap();
223:         }
224:         out.push('\n');
225:     }
226:     out
227: }
228: 
229: fn emit() -> io::Result<Vec<PathBuf>> {
230:     let root = trace_root();
231:     let mut written = Vec::new();
232:     for scenario in scenarios() {
233:         let dir = root.join(scenario.name);
234:         fs::create_dir_all(&dir)?;
235:         for (step, bytes) in scenario.steps {
236:             let path = dir.join(format!("{step}.plpl.hex"));
237:             fs::write(&path, hex_file(scenario.name, step, &bytes))?;
238:             written.push(path);
239:         }
240:     }
241:     Ok(written)
242: }
243: 
244: fn check() -> Result<(), Vec<String>> {
245:     let root = trace_root();
246:     let mut failures = Vec::new();
247:     for scenario in scenarios() {
248:         for (step, bytes) in scenario.steps {
249:             let path = root.join(scenario.name).join(format!("{step}.plpl.hex"));
250:             let expected = hex_file(scenario.name, step, &bytes);
251:             match fs::read_to_string(&path) {
252:                 Ok(actual) if actual == expected => {}
253:                 Ok(_) => failures.push(format!("drift: {}", path.display())),
254:                 Err(_) => failures.push(format!("missing: {}", path.display())),
255:             }
256:         }
257:     }
258:     if failures.is_empty() {
259:         Ok(())
260:     } else {
261:         Err(failures)
262:     }
263: }
264: 
265: fn main() -> io::Result<()> {
266:     match std::env::args().nth(1).as_deref() {
267:         Some("--emit") => {
268:             for path in emit()? {
269:                 println!("wrote {}", path.display());
270:             }
271:         }
272:         Some("--check") => match check() {
273:             Ok(()) => println!("engine trace fixtures are current"),
274:             Err(failures) => {
275:                 for failure in &failures {
276:                     eprintln!("{failure}");
277:                 }
278:                 eprintln!(
279:                     "{} mismatch(es) — run `cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit`",
280:                     failures.len()
281:                 );
282:                 std::process::exit(1);
283:             }
284:         },
285:         other => {
286:             eprintln!("usage: pathland-engine-golden --emit | --check (got {other:?})");
287:             std::process::exit(2);
288:         }
289:     }
290:     Ok(())
291: }

- name: Test workspace
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo test

      - name: Qt renderer headless smoke
        working-directory: lib/rust
        env:
          QT_QPA_PLATFORM: offscreen
          QT_QUICK_BACKEND: software
        run: cargo test -p pathland-render-qt

      # The DOM renderer's constants/token conventions and the cross-renderer SSR
      # golden fixtures are GENERATED from Rust (pathland-ts-codegen /
      # pathland-html-golden). Regenerate them here and fail if the committed
      # files drifted — so a renumbered constant or a changed SSR shape can't land
      # without its TS/fixture counterparts.
      - name: Verify generated TS + golden fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-ts-codegen
          cargo run -p pathland-html-golden -- --emit
          git diff --exit-code -- \
            lib/typescript/src/constants.ts \
            lib/typescript/src/generated \
            lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr

      # The neutral protocol manifest is the machine-readable mirror consumed by
      # non-Rust bindings. Regenerate it from the canonical Rust constants and fail
      # if the committed `spec/protocol.tsv` drifted. The Java job validates its
      # hand-written constants against this file.
      - name: Verify the protocol manifest is current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest
          git -C ../.. diff --exit-code -- spec/protocol.tsv

      # The shared engine traces are emitted by the canonical Rust engine and
      # compared byte-for-byte by the JVM engine test. Verify the committed
      # fixtures have not drifted from the current engine behavior.
      - name: Verify engine trace fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --check

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

      - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: ./check-wasm.sh

      # The Java HTML renderer shim needs the Rust renderer cdylib (the jar embeds
      # it so it travels with the artifact). Build it here and hand it to the java
      # job via an artifact.
      - name: Build the HTML renderer cdylib
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Upload the renderer dylib for the java job
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so
          retention-days: 1

  java:
    name: Java (Maven reactor, JDK ${{ matrix.java }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [rust]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        java: ['17', '21', '25']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Whole-stack floor is Java 17 (maven.compiler.release=17; JNA native binding,
      # thread-local environment); the matrix proves every LTS from 17.
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}
          cache: maven

      # The renderer jar embeds the Rust cdylib (built by the rust job). Restore it
      # into the debug dir the jar-embed step copies.
      - name: Download the Rust renderer dylib
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug

      - name: Test reactor (incl. the SSR web demos)
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: mvn -q -B test

      # Mirror the Dockerfile's Maven selection so the deploy image path is
      # exercised in CI. The deployment module must be selected explicitly: it is
      # not a Maven dependency of the demo, and the runtime extension descriptor
      # validates against it.
      - name: Package the deployable Quarkus demo
        working-directory: lib/java
        run: >-
          mvn -q -B
          -pl pathland-quarkus-demo,pathland-quarkus-deployment -am
          package -Dmaven.test.skip=true

  web-client:
    name: Web client (TypeScript DOM renderer)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

            lib/typescript/src/constants.ts \
            lib/typescript/src/generated \
            lib/typescript/test/fixtures/ssr

      # The neutral protocol manifest is the machine-readable mirror consumed by
      # non-Rust bindings. Regenerate it from the canonical Rust constants and fail
      # if the committed `spec/protocol.tsv` drifted. The Java job validates its
      # hand-written constants against this file.
      - name: Verify the protocol manifest is current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: |
          cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest
          git -C ../.. diff --exit-code -- spec/protocol.tsv

      # The shared engine traces are emitted by the canonical Rust engine and
      # compared byte-for-byte by the JVM engine test. Verify the committed
      # fixtures have not drifted from the current engine behavior.
      - name: Verify engine trace fixtures are current (no drift)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --check

      - name: Build the C ABI (cdylib, used by the Java JNA ring interop / native hosts)
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-core-capi

      - name: no_std / wasm32 direction guard
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: ./check-wasm.sh

      # The Java HTML renderer shim needs the Rust renderer cdylib (the jar embeds
      # it so it travels with the artifact). Build it here and hand it to the java
      # job via an artifact.
      - name: Build the HTML renderer cdylib
        working-directory: lib/rust
        run: cargo build -p pathland-render-html

      - name: Upload the renderer dylib for the java job
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: pathland-render-html-native
          path: lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html.so

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # thread-local environment); the matrix proves every LTS from 17.
      - name: Set up JDK ${{ matrix.java }}
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: ${{ matrix.java }}

      - name: Download the Rust renderer dylib

        with:

      # exercised in CI. The deployment module must be selected explicitly: it is
      # not a Maven dependency of the demo, and the runtime extension descriptor
      # validates against it.

        working-directory: lib/java

          mvn -q -B

          package -Dmaven.test.skip=true

    name: Web client (TypeScript DOM renderer)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

  java:
    name: Publish to Maven Central
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version, java-natives]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.version.outputs.tag }}

      - name: Set up JDK + Maven credentials + GPG
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: '17'
          cache: maven
          server-id: central
          server-username: CENTRAL_USERNAME
          server-password: CENTRAL_PASSWORD
          gpg-private-key: ${{ secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          gpg-passphrase: MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE

      # Maven 3.10 (the runner default since 2026-10-04) writes a
      # `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
      # which central-publishing-maven-plugin bundles and the Portal rejects
      # ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). 3.9.x does not. Pin it here.

          for d in natives/native-*; do
            platform="${d#natives/native-}"
            mkdir -p "lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/$platform"
            cp "$d"/* "lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native/$platform/"
          done
          find lib/java/pathland-render-html/target/native -type f

      # bundles every reactor module (it ignores maven.deploy.skip), and the demos must
      # not be published.

        working-directory: lib/java
        env:
          CENTRAL_USERNAME: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_USERNAME }}
          CENTRAL_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.CENTRAL_PASSWORD }}
          MAVEN_GPG_PASSPHRASE: ${{ secrets.GPG_PASSPHRASE }}
        run: >-
          mvn -B -P release deploy
          -pl '!pathland-demo-views-kotlin,!pathland-desktop-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'

      - name: Collect the published main jars
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist/jars
          for m in pathland-view-core pathland-render-html pathland-server-core \
                   pathland-spring-boot-starter pathland-quarkus \
                   pathland-quarkus-deployment; do
            cp lib/java/"$m"/target/"$m"-*.jar dist/jars/ 2>/dev/null || true
          done
          rm -f dist/jars/*-sources.jar dist/jars/*-javadoc.jar
          ls -la dist/jars

      - name: Upload the main jars
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: jars
          path: dist/jars/*.jar
          if-no-files-found: error

  bump:
    name: Commit the version back to main
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [version, rust, java]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          fetch-depth: 0

                    <artifactId>quarkus-extension-maven-plugin</artifactId>

                    <artifactId>maven-enforcer-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.5.0</version>

                <plugin>

                    <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>${spring-boot.version}</version>
                </plugin>
            </plugins>
        </pluginManagement>
    </build>

    <!-- Run BEFORE an IntelliJ IDE run: refreshes the two layers the IDE cannot rebuild
         itself — the Rust cdylib (cargo) and the DOM bundle (npm build:all) — plus the
         render-html module's embedded dylib (its antrun embed step only runs under Maven,
         NOT under IntelliJ's own build). IntelliJ then compiles the Java modules from its
         module outputs (the pathland modules are imported, so no ~/.m2 is used) and copies
         the refreshed bundle + its dom-renderer.current manifest into target/classes on
         Build Project. Invoke with `mvn -P refresh-ide validate`, then Reload All Maven
         Projects → Build → Run → reload. The bundle is content-hashed
         (dom-renderer-<sha256>.js) so a rebuilt bundle busts the immutable asset cache by
         URL — a normal reload after restart is enough, no hard refresh. -->
    <profiles>
    <!-- Maven Central publishing (`mvn -P release deploy`). Normal builds/tests are
         unaffected: this profile only activates on demand. -->
    <profile>
        <id>release</id>
        <build>
            <plugins>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-source-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.3.1</version>
                    <executions>
                        <execution>
                            <id>attach-sources</id>
                            <goals><goal>jar-no-fork</goal></goals>
                        </execution>
                    </executions>
                </plugin>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-javadoc-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.6.3</version>
                    <configuration>
                        <!-- Central requires a -javadoc jar; disable strict doclint so
                             existing doc comments don't fail the release build. -->
                        <doclint>none</doclint>
                    </configuration>
                    <executions>
                        <execution>
                            <id>attach-javadocs</id>
                            <goals><goal>jar</goal></goals>
                        </execution>
                    </executions>
                </plugin>
                <plugin>
                    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                    <artifactId>maven-gpg-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.2.4</version>
                    <executions>
                        <execution>
                            <id>sign-artifacts</id>
                            <phase>verify</phase>
                            <goals><goal>sign</goal></goals>
                        </execution>
                    </executions>
                </plugin>
                <!-- Uploads the whole reactor to the Sonatype Central Portal as one
                     deployment (auto-published after validation). Credentials come
                     from the `central` server in ~/.m2/settings.xml. -->
                <plugin>

                    <artifactId>exec-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                    <version>3.1.0</version>

                                    <argument>--package=pathland-render-html</argument>
                                </arguments>
                            </configuration>
                        </execution>
                        <execution>

                            <goals><goal>exec</goal></goals>
                            <configuration>

                                <executable>npm</executable>
                                <arguments>
                                    <argument>run</argument>
                                    <argument>build:all</argument>
                                </arguments>
                            </configuration>
                        </execution>
                        <execution>
                            <id>refresh-render-html</id>
                            <phase>validate</phase>
                            <goals><goal>exec</goal></goals>
                            <configuration>
                                <workingDirectory>${session.executionRootDirectory}</workingDirectory>
                                <executable>mvn</executable>
                                <arguments>
                                    <argument>-q</argument>
                                    <argument>-pl</argument>
                                    <argument>pathland-render-html</argument>
                                    <argument>process-resources</argument>
                                </arguments>
                            </configuration>
                        </execution>
                    </executions>
                </plugin>
            </plugins>
        </build>
    </profile>
    </profiles>
</project>

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `CREATE_NODE` | `0x01` | nodeId | componentType (u16, low) | 0 | — | Create a node of `componentType` |
| `DELETE_NODE` | `0x02` | nodeId | 0 | 0 | — | Delete a node and its subtree |
| `INSERT_CHILD` | `0x03` | parentId | childId | index | — | Insert `childId` into `parentId` at `index`; append is `index = u32::MAX` (`APPEND`) |
| `REMOVE_CHILD` | `0x04` | parentId | childId | 0 | — | Remove `childId` from `parentId` |
| `MOVE_CHILD` | `0x05` | parentId | childId | newIndex | — | Move child to `newIndex` (after removal); append is `newIndex = u32::MAX` (`APPEND`) |

### PARAMETER (0x02)

The engine does not emit positions. `PARAMETER` carries the **constraint properties**
that native renderers feed to their own layout — spacing, alignment, FILL/HUG
size hints — plus **styling modifiers** (padding, colors, fonts, borders).

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `SET_PROPERTY` | `0x01` | nodeId | propertyId (u16, low) + valueType (u8, high byte) | value | — | Set a constraint/style property; `value` depends on `valueType` |
| `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x02` | arenaRef (path) | valueType (u8) | value | — | Override a design token; path is an arena string |
| `SET_TEXT` | `0x03` | nodeId | arenaRef (utf8) | 0 | — | Set a node's text content |
| `SET_DATE` | `0x04` | nodeId | days since epoch (I32) | millis of day (U32) | — | Set a node's date value (e.g. a `DATE_PICKER`); see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#date) for the matching `DATE_CHANGED` event |

`SET_PROPERTY` encodes the value type in the **high byte of `B`** (bits 24–31) and the property id in the low two bytes:

```
B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
```

#### Value types

| Value Type | Value | C / value encoding |
|------------|-------|--------------------|
| `U8` | `0x01` | low byte of C |
| `U32` | `0x02` | u32 |
| `I32` | `0x03` | i32 |
=== STRING SECTION ===
| 0x30050 Event arena (bump region, host-owned: event strings)   |
| ...                                                            |
+───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
```

> The event ring is the **host → guest** direction of the shared-memory
> transport: the renderer writes `EVENT`-category opcodes here and the
> guest/app drains them. It uses the same 16-byte slot layout as the main
> (guest → host) ring; both share `slotCount` (same capacity).
>
> The **event arena** is the host-owned bump region that makes strings flow
> **host → guest** over the shared ring: a renderer bump-allocates `TEXT_CHANGED`
> text (and any future string-bearing event payload) here and references it by
> its absolute byte offset — exactly mirroring how the guest uses the guest
> arena for `SET_TEXT` / STRING properties. The host resets its cursor on
> `META::RESET`; if the event arena is full the host applies backpressure
> (drops/stalls the event), mirroring ring backpressure.

### Header block (80 bytes)

| Offset | Size | Field | Producer | Description |
|--------|------|-------|----------|-------------|
| 0x00 | 4 | `magic` | — | `0x504C504C` (`PLPL`) |
| 0x04 | 2 | `version` | — | Wire protocol version (1) |
| 0x06 | 4 | `ringOffset` | — | Byte offset of the ring region |
| 0x0A | 4 | `ringBytes` | — | Byte length of the ring region |
| 0x0E | 4 | `slotCount` | — | Number of ring slots (power of two) |
| 0x12 | 4 | `arenaOffset` | — | Byte offset of the arena region |
| 0x16 | 4 | `arenaBytes` | — | Byte length of the arena region |
| 0x1A | 4 | `arenaCursor` | guest | Next free byte in the arena |
| 0x1E | 4 | `readCursor` | host | Ring slot the host has consumed up to |
| 0x22 | 4 | `writeCursor` | guest | Ring slot the guest has written up to |
| 0x26 | 4 | `frameCount` | guest | Monotonic completed-frame counter |
| 0x2A | 4 | `eventRingOffset` | — | Byte offset of the host→guest event ring region |
| 0x2E | 4 | `eventRingBytes` | — | Byte length of the event ring region |
| 0x32 | 4 | `eventSlotCount` | — | Event ring slot count (power of two; = `slotCount`) |
| 0x36 | 4 | `eventReadCursor` | guest | Event ring slot the guest has consumed up to |
| 0x3A | 4 | `eventWriteCursor` | host | Event ring slot the host has written up to |
| 0x40 | 4 | `eventArenaOffset` | — | Byte offset of the host→guest event arena region |
| 0x44 | 4 | `eventArenaBytes` | — | Byte length of the event arena region |
| 0x48 | 4 | `eventArenaCursor` | host | Next free byte in the event arena |

### Ring buffer

- Contiguous array of **16-byte slots**; `slotCount` is a **power of two** (wrap via mask, no modulo).
- **Producer** (guest) writes at `writeCursor`, then advances `writeCursor` and increments `frameCount` at frame end.
- **Consumer** (host) reads from `readCursor` up to `writeCursor`; after draining a frame it advances `readCursor`.
- **Backpressure**: the producer must not advance `writeCursor` past `readCursor` (ring full). The producer SHOULD flush a frame before the ring is full.
- **Frame boundary detection**: the host watches `frameCount`. When it advances, exactly one frame (all slots from the previously consumed `readCursor` to the current `writeCursor`) is complete.

### Event ring (host → guest)

- The **host** (renderer) is the producer: it writes `EVENT`-category opcodes at `eventWriteCursor`.
- The **guest** (app/engine) is the consumer: it reads from `eventReadCursor` up to `eventWriteCursor`, then advances `eventReadCursor`.
- Events are raw inputs and are consumed as soon as they are written (no frame batching); `eventFrameCount` is not required.
- Backpressure mirrors the main ring: the host must not advance `eventWriteCursor` past `eventReadCursor`.

### Arena

- A pre-allocated **bump region** for variable-length data (strings, token paths).
- Every arena entry is **self-describing**: `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`.
- Opcodes reference entries by their **byte offset** (`arenaRef`), so an entry's length is read directly from the arena — all opcodes stay 16 bytes.
- The guest advances `arenaCursor` monotonically (no free-list, no fragmentation). The arena MAY be reset via `META::RESET`.

### Event arena (host → guest)

The event arena is the **host-owned mirror** of the arena, giving the shared-memory
transport a host → guest string section so strings flow **both ways on all
transports**:

- The **host** (renderer) bump-allocates event string payloads here (e.g. the
  new text of a `TEXT_CHANGED`) and references them by their **absolute byte
  offset** in the event opcode — the same `SET_TEXT` shared-memory convention
  used in the guest arena.
- The **guest** resolves the text from the event arena region when draining
  events (`EVENT::TEXT_CHANGED`).
- Entries share the same self-describing `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]` layout as
  the guest arena.
- The host advances `eventArenaCursor` monotonically and resets it on
  `META::RESET`; a full event arena is backpressure (the host drops/stalls the
  event until the guest drains or a reset lands).
- Over the **network**, host → guest string payloads use the batch's string
  section with *relative* offsets instead (see [Transport](#transport)) — the
  same dual absolute/relative convention as `SET_TEXT`.

---

## Colors

Literal colors are **sRGB** (IEC 61966-2-1, D65 white point), packed as `0xAARRGGBB`:

- `AA`: alpha (0x00 transparent – 0xFF opaque)
- `RR`: red, `GG`: green, `BB`: blue

Stored little-endian in a `u32` payload. A color **property** may alternatively carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path instead of a literal (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)); semantic token resolution and theme adaptation remain **renderer-owned**.

---
```

# pathland-protocol-manifest — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 1, 2026

Emits the target-neutral wire protocol manifest (`spec/protocol.tsv`) from the
canonical Rust constants (`pathland_core::constants`). It emits only data:
`kind`, `group`, `name`, `value`. It contains no target-language source,
package names, class structure, or formatting.

## Implemented

- Categories, components, commands, field ids, flags, listener bits, size
  sentinels, value types, property ids, and `property → value_type` mappings.
- Deterministic tab-separated output with a generated-file header.
- `cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest` regenerates the committed manifest.
- CI regenerates and fails on `spec/protocol.tsv` drift.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Enum wire-code tables (alignment, shape kind, control state, …) are not yet in
  the manifest; they remain hand-mirrored in the language bindings.
- The manifest is emitted from explicit Rust constant bindings rather than
  reflection; adding a new Rust constant deliberately requires adding its
  manifest row so the output stays ordered and documented.
=== ENGINE TRACES README ===

Generated by `pathland-engine-golden` from the canonical Rust engine. Do not
edit the `.plpl.hex` files by hand.

lowercase hex. `#` lines are metadata/comments.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Shared helpers for the Pathland demo scripts. Source this file; it defines
# $ROOT (the repository root) and the prerequisite-build helpers each demo uses.

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"

# Build the generated HTML base design and sync it into the renderer crate.
build_design() {
  if [[ ! -d "$ROOT/design/node_modules" ]]; then
    (cd "$ROOT/design" && npm ci)
  fi
  (cd "$ROOT/design" && npm run build)
  "$ROOT/scripts/sync-design-css.sh"
}

# Build the Rust HTML renderer cdylib (embedded in the Java pathland-render-html jar).
build_rust_html() {
  build_design
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-render-html)
}

# Build the Rust dylibs the desktop demos link: the core ring (libpathland_core)
# and the GTK4 renderer (libpathland_gtk).
build_gtk_dylibs() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-gtk)
}

# Build the Rust dylibs the Qt desktop demo links: the core ring
# (libpathland_core) and the Qt Quick renderer (libpathland_qt).
build_qt_dylibs() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/rust" && cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-qt)
}

# Install the Java reactor (everything except the web demos, which are launched
# separately; they are not required to launch the other demos).
java_install() {
  (cd "$ROOT/lib/java" && mvn -q install -DskipTests \
    -pl '!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo')
}=== scripts ===
